It is popular but has caused some risks.
explanation: Many cyclists 'have welcomed the lane', yet there have been near misses at crossings. Nothing suggests restricted hours or a closure.

text: Listen to an announcement at the campus gym.
script: W: Good evening, members of the Campus Gym. I have some news about next week.
W: The swimming pool will be closed on Monday and Tuesday because workers are cleaning the water. The pool will open again on Wednesday at six in the morning.

W: The weight room and the running track will be open as usual. On Tuesday, we will also have a free yoga class at seven in the evening in Room two. Bring your own mat, or ask for one at the front desk.
W: Thank you, and enjoy your workout.

stem: Why will the pool be closed?
options: The water is too cold for swimmers.
The gym is closed for a holiday.
A swimming class is using it.
Workers are cleaning it.
explanation: The speaker says the pool is closed 'because workers are cleaning the water'. The weight room and track stay open, so the gym is not closed.

stem: What can members do on Tuesday evening?
options: Swim from six in the morning.
Join a free yoga class.
Buy a new yoga mat.
Run in the weight room.
explanation: She says there is 'a free yoga class at seven in the evening'. The pool opens again on Wednesday, not Tuesday.

text: Listen to an announcement in a school cafeteria.
script: M: Hello, everyone. This is Mr. Lopez from the cafeteria. I have a short message about lunch.

M: Starting tomorrow, we will have a new salad bar next to the sandwich counter. You can make your own salad with vegetables, cheese, and eggs. A small salad costs three dollars, and a large one costs five dollars.
M: We will also stop selling soda. Instead, you can buy fruit juice or bottled water for one dollar.
M: If you have an idea for the menu, please write it on a card and put it in the box near the door. Thank you.

stem: What is new in the cafeteria starting tomorrow?
options: A sandwich counter.
A free fruit juice.
A salad bar.
A card box at the door.
explanation: Mr. Lopez says there will be 'a new salad bar next to the sandwich counter'. The sandwich counter already exists, and the juice costs one dollar.

stem: What should students do if they have a menu idea?
options: Put a card in a box.
Tell the cashier at the salad bar.
Send an email to Mr. Lopez.
Ask for a larger salad.
explanation: The speaker says 'write it on a card and put it in the box near the door'. He does not mention email or telling the cashier.

text: Listen to a voicemail message from a tutoring center.
script: W: Hello, this is Rosa from the Tutoring Center, calling for Hamza.
W: You asked for help with your math homework. A tutor named Ben has time on Thursday afternoon. He can meet you at three o'clock in Room one oh five of the library. The session will last one hour.
W: Please bring your math book and the homework you want to work on. If you can't come at three, please call me back at five five five, oh one two three. Or you can send an email to the center.
W: I hope to hear from you soon. Goodbye.

stem: Why is Rosa calling Hamza?
options: To offer him a tutor time.
To give him his math grade.
To ask him to be a tutor.
To return his math book.
explanation: Rosa says Hamza asked for help with math, and a tutor 'has time on Thursday afternoon'. She does not talk about grades or ask him to teach.

stem: What should Hamza do if three o'clock is not good for him?
options: Go to the library without calling.
Call Rosa back.
Bring his book on Friday.
Meet Ben in Room two.
explanation: Rosa says 'If you can't come at three, please call me back'. The meeting place is Room one oh five, and Friday is not mentioned.

text: Listen to an announcement at a bookstore.
script: W: Welcome to the University Bookstore. Please listen to some news about our special sale.
W: This week, all notebooks and pens are twenty percent cheaper. If you buy three notebooks, you will get a free pen. The sale ends on Sunday.
W: We also have a table of used textbooks near the door. These books cost half the price of new books, but they go quickly, so come early.
W: If you pay with a student card, you can get a small discount on everything. The store is open from nine to six every day. Thank you for shopping with us.

stem: What is on sale this week?
options: Used textbooks and bags.
Student cards and pens.
Only new textbooks.
Notebooks and pens.
explanation: The speaker says 'all notebooks and pens are twenty percent cheaper'. Used books are always half price, not part of this sale.

stem: How can a shopper get a free pen?
options: By buying a used textbook.
By paying with cash on Sunday.
By buying three notebooks.
By coming before nine.
explanation: She says 'If you buy three notebooks, you will get a free pen'. A student card gives a different small discount.

text: Listen to an announcement from an environmental science professor.
script: W: Hello, everyone. I have some changes to share about the stream study project.

W: We were going to collect water samples this Saturday, but the forecast shows heavy rain, and the stream will be too high to enter safely. We will collect the samples next Saturday instead, at the same time and place.
W: This delay actually helps us. Since we will have a week of data about rainfall, we can compare the samples to the amount of rain. So please keep a record of the rain in your own neighborhood.
W: You can use a simple cup and a ruler. Bring your record to class on Monday, and we will combine everyone's numbers.

stem: Why is the sampling trip being delayed?
options: The stream could be unsafe.
The professor is away on Saturday.
Some equipment has not arrived.
Students asked for more preparation time.
explanation: The professor says the stream 'will be too high to enter safely'. She does not mention equipment or student requests.

stem: What does the professor want students to do this week?
options: Collect samples from a nearby stream.
Measure the rain where they live.
Write a report about the forecast.
Buy a rain gauge for the class.
explanation: She asks them to 'keep a record of the rain in your own neighborhood' using 'a simple cup and a ruler'. The samples are collected next Saturday, and no purchase is needed.

text: Listen to a phone message asking for research volunteers.
script: M: Hi, this is Kenji from the Language Learning Lab. We are looking for students who speak Spanish as their first language.

M: Our study looks at how people learn English pronunciation. If you join, you will listen to short English sentences through headphones and repeat them into a microphone. Then we will ask you to read a short story aloud.
M: The session takes about forty-five minutes and is held in the Humanities Building. We pay fifteen dollars in cash at the end.
M: We have openings every weekday afternoon next week. Please reply to this message with the day you prefer, and I'll confirm the time.

stem: Who is the lab trying to find?
options: Teachers of English pronunciation.
Students who are learning Spanish.
Native Spanish speakers.
Visitors from other universities.
explanation: Kenji says they want 'students who speak Spanish as their first language'. Learners of Spanish would not fit, and no teachers or visitors are mentioned.

stem: What will volunteers do first?
options: Take a test on grammar rules.
Read a story aloud to the researcher.
Fill out a form about their studies.
Repeat English sentences they hear.
explanation: They 'will listen to short English sentences through headphones and repeat them'. Reading the story comes afterward, and no form or grammar test is mentioned.

text: Listen to a notice on a museum tour.
script: W: Good afternoon, and thank you for joining the Heritage House tour. This house was built in eighteen ninety and was once the home of a wealthy merchant family.
W: The tour lasts about an hour. We will begin in the kitchen, then visit the dining room and the library on the ground floor, and finish in the bedrooms upstairs.
W: Please do not touch the furniture or the wallpaper, as they are very old. Photographs are allowed, but without flash. The upstairs rooms are narrow, so groups will go up in two parts.
W: If you need a rest, there are benches in the garden. Questions are welcome at any time.

stem: Where will the tour end?
options: In the library downstairs.
In the kitchen.
In the bedrooms.
In the garden.
explanation: The guide says the tour will 'finish in the bedrooms upstairs'. The kitchen is the start, and the library is visited before the bedrooms.

stem: Why will groups go upstairs in two parts?
options: The furniture needs protection.
The rooms are narrow.
The tour has become too long.
Some visitors want to take photographs.
explanation: She says 'The upstairs rooms are narrow, so groups will go up in two parts'. Furniture protection is the reason for not touching, not for splitting the group.

text: Listen to a safety announcement for a science laboratory.
script: M: Welcome to the first meeting of Chemistry Lab. Before we begin, I need to explain the safety rules.

M: First, wear goggles and a lab coat at all times. Long hair must be tied back, and open shoes are not allowed. If your clothes are not suitable, you will be asked to leave and come back for the next session.
M: Second, never taste or smell chemicals directly. If you need to smell something, wave the air toward your face with your hand.
M: Finally, if an accident happens, tell me immediately. Do not try to hide it, even if it seems small. A quick report keeps everyone safe.

stem: What will happen to a student wearing open shoes?
options: The student will be given special shoes.
The student will receive a lab coat.
The student will do the lab alone.
He will have to return later.
explanation: The instructor says anyone in unsuitable clothes 'will be asked to leave and come back for the next session'. No special equipment is offered.

stem: What does the instructor say about small accidents?
options: They should be reported right away.
They are not important to record.
They can be fixed without telling him.
They are only a problem for the goggles.
explanation: He says 'tell me immediately. Do not try to hide it, even if it seems small'. Waving air toward your face is about smelling chemicals, not accidents.

text: Listen to an announcement from an economics professor.
script: M: Before we end, a word about the group presentations. I've seen the proposals, and most of you chose famous companies. That's understandable, but it's not what I had hoped for.

M: A company everyone knows is a company everyone has opinions about, which makes it difficult to say anything new. I'd encourage you to consider a small local business, because there you can interview the owner and collect your own data.
M: I won't force anyone to change. Groups that stay with a famous company can do so, but I'll expect a clearer argument from them, since the information is so easy to find.
M: Send me your final choice by Friday, and I'll confirm it.

stem: What is the professor's attitude toward the proposals?
options: He is delighted with the creativity.
He is a bit let down.
He is worried about the deadline.
He is angry about a missed assignment.
explanation: He says the choices are understandable but 'not what I had hoped for'. He does not complain about deadlines or missed work.

stem: What does the professor imply about groups who keep a famous company?
options: They will be judged by a higher standard.
They will receive a lower grade automatically.
They will not be allowed to present.
They must interview the company's owner.
explanation: He will 'expect a clearer argument from them, since the information is so easy to find'. He does not penalize them automatically, and owner interviews are the benefit of a small business.

text: Listen to a message from a museum volunteer coordinator.
script: W: Hello, this is Elena from the Natural History Museum, calling about your volunteer application.
W: We were pleased to read about your experience as a teaching assistant. Our difficulty is that our weekend positions, which are the ones most students prefer, are already filled for this season.

W: What we do have are openings on weekday mornings, working with school groups. The hours are less convenient, but the work is more interesting, since you would lead the activity tables yourself rather than only directing visitors.
W: If you think you could manage that, please tell me by Wednesday, and we can set up an orientation.

stem: Why does the coordinator describe the weekday openings as 'less convenient'?
options: They involve too much paperwork.
They are far from the museum entrance.
They clash with class times.
They are unpaid for the whole season.
explanation: The weekday mornings are contrasted with weekends, which students prefer, so the hours are harder for students. Her next sentence about interesting work shows that the job itself is not the problem.

stem: What is Elena's main purpose?
options: To ask for more teaching experience.
To reject the application completely.
To invite the applicant to a weekend event.
To offer an alternative to the applicant.
explanation: The preferred weekend positions are full, so she suggests weekday mornings and asks for a reply by Wednesday. She praises the applicant's experience, so she is not rejecting it.

text: Listen to an announcement about a campus bridge renovation.
script: M: This is a notice for everyone who crosses the footbridge between the science and arts buildings. Some of you may have thought it would stay open during the renovation. I'm sorry to say that won't be possible.
M: The bridge will be closed from the fifteenth of May to the end of August. The old surface needs to be removed entirely, and the workers can't do that safely with people walking above.
M: A path along the river will be marked as an alternative. It adds about ten minutes, so those with classes in both buildings should allow extra time in the fall.
M: On a positive note, the new bridge will be wider and will include a space for bicycles.

stem: What can be inferred about the old bridge?
options: It will be sold to a private owner.
It will remain open on weekends.
It was damaged by bicycle traffic.
It cannot stay in use.
explanation: The 'old surface needs to be removed entirely', which means it cannot simply be repaired while open. The announcement says nothing about its sale or about bicycles damaging it.

stem: Who will be most affected by the river path?
options: Cyclists who use the bridge at night.
Students crossing between buildings.
Workers who live near the river.
Visitors to the science building.
explanation: The path 'adds about ten minutes, so those with classes in both buildings should allow extra time'. The announcement does not single out cyclists, workers or visitors.

text: Listen to a talk by a tour leader before a cave visit.
script: W: Before we go underground, here is what to expect. The cave stays at about twelve degrees all year, so it will feel cold in summer and mild in winter. Most of you are dressed correctly, but a few might regret leaving sweaters in the bus.

W: The passage is narrow in places, and the ceiling is low. Anyone who is nervous in enclosed spaces should speak to me now, not halfway through. There is no shame in that, and our visitor center has a model of the cave with a film.
W: I'll also ask you to stay behind me. The stones are slippery, and the formations take thousands of years to grow, so even a gentle touch can leave a permanent mark.

stem: Why does the leader suggest speaking to her now?
options: The visit begins in a few minutes.
The model is not available later.
It is difficult to leave once inside.
The film cannot be shown after the tour.
explanation: She says to speak 'now, not halfway through' and mentions that the passage is narrow, so leaving later would be hard. The model and film are available at the visitor center.

stem: What does the leader imply about visitors who have no sweater?
options: They may feel cold underground.
They cannot enter the cave.
They should wait on the bus.
They will be given extra clothing.
explanation: She says 'a few might regret leaving sweaters in the bus', since the cave stays cool. No extra clothing or ban is mentioned.
